title: HTTP last-response-header helpers
summary: PHP 8.4 adds http_get_last_response_headers() and http_clear_last_response_headers() for the HTTP stream wrapper.
new_code_policy: Call these helpers unconditionally only when the PHP feature ceiling is at least 8.4. Capture headers immediately after the HTTP stream-wrapper request; retain the captured array before clearing shared state.
existing_code_policy: Keep the capability-checked, same-request-scope fallback in core.http_response_header while supporting PHP 8.2 or 8.3. Raising the floor to 8.4 permits the helpers, but does not make moving header reads across requests safe.
guideline: On PHP 8.4 or later, retrieve the HTTP stream wrapper's last response headers with http_get_last_response_headers() and clear stored headers explicitly with http_clear_last_response_headers().
details: The PHP 8.4.0 UPGRADING New Functions / Standard section introduces both helpers. http_get_last_response_headers(): ?array returns the stored raw response-header lines, or null when none are stored; http_clear_last_response_headers(): void clears that state. These helpers concern the HTTP stream wrapper, not cURL. The state is not local to the function that made the request: capture it immediately before another request can replace it. The example requires a PHP 8.4 floor, assumes $url is an HTTP URL, and owns the request/capture/clear sequence. It clears before the request and again in finally; clearing also affects other code reading the shared last-response state. The captured array remains available after clearing. No status-line parsing is performed here. The separate core.http_response_header rule retains the old variable's PHP 8.5 deprecation contract.

after: // Requires PHP 8.4+; this code owns the last-response-header state.

notes: Qualification on main 97be19e: list-rules --php=8.4 --kind=feature --all --json has no HTTP helper feature rule; explain core.http_response_header retains kind=deprecated, introduced_in=null and deprecated_in=8.5. The new rule exposes API availability without inferring a feature contract from deprecation prose.

Guidance only: verification.phpcompatibility intentionally remains empty. Issue #18 records a historical singular/plural-name defect in the pinned analyzer; this slice does not claim a new analyzer probe, add a mapping, or change its pin. Zero findings would not prove compatibility.

PHP manual cross-check on 2026-09-26: https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.http-get-last-response-headers.php and https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.http-clear-last-response-headers.php document PHP 8.4.0 availability, the nullable array returned by get, and the clearing behavior.
